QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_21

question.text: Himachal Debt Fund (Cat II close-ended) has a scheduled tenure expiry in September 2025. The Manager wishes to extend tenure by 2 years to complete portfolio harvest. What investor approval threshold must be obtained, and up to how many years (for a non-LVF scheme)?

answer.text: 51% of investors by number; extension up to 1 year.
Two-thirds of unit holders by value; extension up to 2 years.
75% of investors by value; extension up to 5 years.
Unanimous consent; extension up to 3 years.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12 CTR disclosure and Regulation 13 framework: fund tenure of a close-ended AIF can be extended for up to 2 years after seeking approval from TWO-THIRDS of unit holders by value of their investment. (Large Value Funds may extend up to 5 years, subject to 2/3 consent — added by 2024 Fourth Amendment.) The Trap: 51% by number ignores 'by value' requirement. 75%-by-value is the winding-up / material-change threshold (adjacent-rule trap). Unanimous is not required. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C identical. XIX-A distributor exam may test the LP-side of this — when can the client exit if they disagree with extension? Manager's Pro-Tip: Run the 2/3 vote early — ideally 6 months before tenure expiry. If you fail to get 2/3, you enter the 1-year Liquidation Period, which is more time-constrained. A pre-vote roadshow to top LPs is time well spent.
